issues.description: The result says a code’s numerical Hamming distance is preserved only when the ambient bijection is an isometry (or the metric is transported). This is false as a necessary condition for one code or its minimum distance: an ambient permutation can fix every codeword while non-isometrically permuting words outside the code.
issues.fix: State instead that an ambient isometry guarantees preservation, and preserving all ambient pairwise Hamming distances is exactly the isometry condition. A particular code’s minimum distance may coincide accidentally under a non-isometric permutation. Retain the correct repetition-code counterexample as proof that categorical composition preservation alone gives no distance guarantee.
issues.resolution: The revised result explicitly distinguishes ambient isometry from accidental preservation of one code/minimum distance.

issues.description: Some verifier expressions are tautological rather than independent evaluations: July contact check includes a*a==a*a, and August Hardy check consists of constant equalities. The mathematical proofs in the entries are sound, but these lines provide less evidence than the check labels suggest.
issues.fix: For the Hardy example, independently integrate the two piecewise polynomial halves to compute zero mean, pairing and oscillation; verify the atom bound from interval length. For contact scaling, independently expand the pullback’s dz and y dx coefficients and compare with the scaled form. Alternatively label those parts as textual proof audits rather than computational identity checks.
issues.resolution: The contact check now computes the covector pullback with a Jacobian independently; the Hardy check integrates the two affine pieces exactly.

issues.description: The final two-sided finite seminorm-difference statement tacitly assumes b has finite BMO seminorm. For a merely locally integrable function both seminorms can be infinite, so their difference need not be defined.
issues.fix: Explicitly assume b∈BMO for the statement | ||b+e||_BMO−||b||_BMO |≤2ε. The one-sided extended-valued inequality and local atom bound need no change.
issues.resolution: The finite two-sided seminorm statement now explicitly assumes b∈BMO and concludes b+e∈BMO.

approved_scopes.finding: Measurable conjugacy, BSC capacity and relabeling, scalar PID characteristic polynomial/feedthrough, dimensionless logarithms, ideal positive algebra and diffusion/observation identities are correct under the declared hypotheses.
The path-three incidence convention is explicit. BBᵀ has eigenvalues one and three, giving the complete Dirac spectrum 0,±1,±√3 and nullity one. Orientation changes are orthogonal conjugacies.
The characteristic-two tangent direction is nontrivial and obstructed modulo η³. The representing fixed-characteristic relation k[[t]]/(t²) and mixed-characteristic qualification 2t+t² are correct.
All four BV bracket formulas have the correct degree-minus-one signs for the stated convention. Δ²=0 and order at most two justify the classical odd Jacobi input; 216 finite Jacobi triples also pass.

The local Hardy atom estimate is valid and attained by the stated example. The global BMO and Hardy-vs-Sobolev limits are preserved. The 2ε perturbation constant is valid, even though it is not claimed optimal.

Photon number density times hc/λ has energy-density units; directed, net isotropic and one-sided isotropic flux are correctly distinguished, including cu/4. Power-law ratio and finite-data nonidentifiability claims are appropriately conditional.

Remaining arithmetic, formal-series, differential-form, motivic-realization, monodromy, intersection-cohomology, contact, persistence, covariance, modular, semidirect-product, symmetry-counterexample, finite-field zeta, operadic-deformation and Gauss-norm statements were read and found mathematically sound within their explicit toy/classical scope. No RH, physical-validation or full-geometry conclusion is inferred from finite verification.
